_comment: Acronyms that en-US does not ask to be spelled out. Detection of undefined acronyms is productive (shape: two to six capital letters, optionally a plural -s), so this list only excuses; it never finds. The seed is the example list of the Federal Plain Language Guidelines (2011, p. 33) for abbreviations 'that have entered common usage': IBM, ATM, BMW, CIA (PhD is not all capitals and is never matched). The rest are Lucid additions of the same kind and are marked so. A longer list would raise precision and hide acronyms a given reader does not know; that trade is the author's, not the tool's.
